topic: Special needs child adoption tax deduction
what_it_gives: Parents can deduct $2,000 per year for each special needs child adopted who is dependent and under age 21.
quote: Two thousand dollars for each adopted special needs child who is: (i) dependent upon and receiving chief support from the taxpayer; (ii) under the age of twenty-one; and (iii) enrolled in an accredited school or college or is incapable of self-support because of mental or physical defects.

topic: Autism spectrum disorder insurance coverage (Ryan's Law)
what_it_gives: Health insurance must cover treatment of autism spectrum disorder; plans cannot deny coverage based on autism diagnosis; eligible children under 16 get up to $50,000 per year for behavioral therapy.
quote: A health insurance plan as defined in this section must provide coverage for the treatment of autism spectrum disorder. Coverage provided under this section is limited to treatment that is prescribed by the insured's treating medical doctor in accordance with a treatment plan. With regards to a health insurance plan as defined in this section an insurer may not deny or refuse to issue coverage on, refuse to contract with, or refuse to renew or refuse to reissue or otherwise terminate or restrict coverage on an individual solely because the individual is diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder.

topic: Continuation of coverage for disabled dependent children
what_it_gives: Insurance cannot terminate a dependent child's coverage at the age limit if the child is incapable of self-supporting employment by reason of disability and is dependent on the parent.
quote: An individual hospital or medical expense insurance policy, hospital service plan contract, or medical service plan contract delivered or issued for delivery in this State which provides that coverage of a dependent child terminates upon attainment of the limiting age for dependent children specified in the policy or contract shall also provide in substance that attainment of the limiting age does not operate to terminate the coverage of the child while the child is and continues to be both (a) incapable of self-sustaining employment by reason of intellectual disability or physical handicap and (b) chiefly dependent upon the policyholder or subscriber for support and maintenance.

topic: Educational rights transfer to adult students with disabilities
what_it_gives: When a student receiving special education turns 18, all special education rights (IEP decisions) automatically transfer from parents to the student unless the student delegates rights or is declared incapacitated.
quote: When a student who is eligible for special education under the Individuals with Disabilities Education Act "IDEA", 20 U.S.C. Section 1411, et seq., reaches age eighteen or is emancipated by a court of competent jurisdiction, all rights accorded to the student's parents under this article transfer to the student except as provided in Sections 59-33-330 and 59-33-340.

topic: Educational representative designation for communication-impaired students
what_it_gives: If a student with disabilities cannot communicate education preferences even with accommodations, a parent or representative can be designated to make IEP decisions (testing can occur as early as 60 days before age 18).
quote: An adult student who is eligible for special education and has not been determined to be incapacitated pursuant to Article 5, Title 62, may be identified as incapable of communicating, with or without reasonable accommodations, his wishes, interests, or preferences with respect to his educational program as early as sixty calendar days before his eighteenth birthday or sixty-five business days before an eligibility meeting, if he is undergoing initial eligibility for special education services, and also may have an educational representative designated.

what_it_gives: SC law defines 'adult' as 18+ or younger if married/emancipated; allows alternatives to guardianship (powers of attorney, healthcare agents) for managing affairs of incapacitated persons.
quote: "Adult" means an individual who has attained the age of eighteen or who, if under eighteen, is married or has been emancipated by a court of competent jurisdiction.

topic: Health care power of attorney for disabled adult children
what_it_gives: Parents can designate themselves as healthcare agents for adult children with disabilities through a durable power of attorney, allowing decision-making authority without full guardianship.
quote: A health care power of attorney is a durable power of attorney. Statutory provisions that refer to a durable power of attorney or judicial interpretations of the law relating to durable powers of attorney apply to a health care power of attorney to the extent that they are not inconsistent with this part.

topic: DDSN services purpose and family support
what_it_gives: State recognizes importance of family role in disability services and commitment to provide services enabling family members to care for relatives with disabilities; admission to DDSN does not reduce parental rights.
quote: The State recognizes the importance of the role of parents and families in shaping services for persons with intellectual disability, related disabilities, head injuries, or spinal cord injuries as well as the importance of providing services to families to enable them to care for a family member with these disabilities. Admission to services of the Office of Intellectual and Developmental Disabilities does not terminate or reduce the rights and responsibilities of parents.

topic: Community-based school attendance for DDSN clients
what_it_gives: Placement in DDSN services does not prevent a person from attending regular community public school classes if they qualify for those classes.
quote: Placement of a person with intellectual disability, a related disability, head injury, or spinal cord injury in a program of the Office of Intellectual and Developmental Disabilities does not preclude his attendance in community-based public school classes when the individual qualifies for the classes.

topic: Insurance coverage for children placed for adoption
what_it_gives: Health plans must provide coverage for adopted children or children placed for adoption under same terms as biological children; cannot exclude based on preexisting conditions.
quote: If an individual or group health plan provides coverage for dependent children of participants or beneficiaries, the plan shall provide benefits to dependent children placed with participants or beneficiaries for adoption under the same terms and conditions as apply to the natural, dependent children of the participants and beneficiaries, irrespective of whether the adoption has become final. A group health plan may not restrict coverage under the plan of a dependent child adopted by a participant or beneficiary or placed with a participant or beneficiary for adoption solely on the basis of a preexisting condition of the child.

what_it_gives: State guarantees special education services including special classes, speech therapy, braille services, transportation, instructional materials, therapy, and psychological services for children with disabilities.
quote: "Special education services" shall mean, but not be limited to, special classes, special housing, homebound instruction, special rental facilities, braillists and typists for visually handicapped children, transportation, maintenance, instructional materials, therapy, professional consultant services, psychological services, itinerant services and resource services.

what_it_gives: Schools must use universal screening process to identify students at risk for reading difficulties including dyslexia; screening occurs 3 times per year in K-1st grade and as needed in 2nd grade.
quote: Beginning with the 2019-2020 School Year, to the extent funding is provided or that approved screening tools are available at no cost, a local school district shall use the universal screening process to screen each student in the district who is in kindergarten through first grade three times each school year and as needed in second grade as outlined in the district's universal screening procedures, and any other student as required by the department, for reading difficulties, including dyslexia, and the need for intervention.

topic: Mediation before special education due process hearings
what_it_gives: State Board of Education provides free mediation process available to parents and school districts before due process hearings; mediation is voluntary and does not compromise parent's right to due process.
quote: The State Board of Education shall establish a mediation process as a part of the "due process" provision required in accordance with Public Law 94-142. If all parties agree, mediation will be used before any due process hearings required by Public Law 94-142 or at any time during the due process procedures. During discussions of the mediation process with parents, it must be clearly stated that the right of the parents or the school district to due process is in no way compromised by agreeing to mediation and that neither parents nor the school district are bound by the outcomes of mediation.
